text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do: Replace the current prompt-review system with a shared log that records every prompt change with timestamps. This makes decisions transparent and auditable—why we changed a prompt and what outcome we expected—without relying on scattered notes or memory. Trade-off: It adds a small upfront cost to log each change, but saves time and mistakes later by making the history obvious.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t clutter—it’s that a decision log alone can’t reconstruct *why* a change worked (or failed). A shared log just records tweaks; it doesn’t tie outcomes to the prompt’s actual performance in production. Settle it by running an A/B test: log changes *and* measure their impact on a clear metric (e.g., task success rate) before declaring the system improved.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do: Add a one-sentence “expected impact” field to every prompt change in the shared log. This forces us to state the outcome we’re aiming for up front, so later we can check whether the change actually delivered. Trade-off: it adds a few seconds per entry, but that’s cheaper than guessing why a prompt later.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: A one-sentence "expected impact" field won’t fix the core problem—it’s still a guess written after the fact. The real risk is that we confuse *stated intent* with *measured outcome*. Settle it by pairing every log entry with a live metric: if the change doesn’t move the needle in production within 48 hours, the log entry is invalidated.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Pair every prompt change log entry with a live production metric and a one-sentence expected impact—then auto-flag mismatches between stated intent and measured outcome. Result: a transparent, auditable log where every tweak is tied to real data. Owner: Gauge.
